correctness.rationale: Writing ell_i=h_i-1, a coordinate reset at t followed by ell_i nonresets gives exactly one qualifying marker, with t from 1 to n-ell_i and probability (1-q)q^ell_i. Starting from zero, the only additional way to reach h_i is the initial run of h_i successes, of probability q^h_i=O(1/n) in the window. Each indicator depends on its closed update interval and is independent jointly of all indicators on disjoint intervals. Same-type overlapping distinct markers and distinct types started at the same time are impossible. For an X reset and a later Y reset at lag 1≤k≤ell_X, the later reset also serves as one forced X success; L=min(ell_X-k,ell_Y) simultaneous successes have mass a=2q-1 instead of q^2. The resulting joint mass is (1-q)^2 q^(ell_X+ell_Y-1)(a/q^2)^L. Independently enumerated unequal-length examples at q=3/4 with integer weights 1,1,2, including ell_X=4, ell_Y=1, k=1 (18/1024) and k=4 (81/4096), agree. The window bounds the difference of lengths and a/q^2<1 gives an O(1) geometric sum in each direction, so the distinct-neighbor joint term is O(1/n). The product term including self pairs is O(log n/n), from O(n log n) pairs each O(n^-2); the term for dependence on the outside is zero. The standard local-dependence Poisson process bound at individual indices, followed by contraction under summing the two disjoint color classes, gives the claimed vector TV estimate and independent Poisson means. Simultaneous absence plus the initial-run error and the O(log n/n) mean adjustments yield exactly the uniform height formulas. The lattice limits are interpreted along subsequences with convergent intensities, not as a continuously centered weak limit. The frozen checker was read, not executed; its marker-pair loop uses equal lengths, while the independent check above and, decisively, the product argument cover unequal thresholds.
residual_risks: Constants are for fixed q,c,C; no uniform parameter-endpoint or outside-window claim.

evidence: Scalar height asymptotics do not imply asymptotic independence. The proof here evaluates the full cross-coordinate neighboring-marker mass through the factor ((2q-1)/q^2)^L, and sums it uniformly over shifted unequal intervals, treating mutually exclusive reset times separately.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: General Poisson approximation supplies the framework; it does not certify that overlapping-coordinate clusters are negligible. The exact joint overlap and controlled neighbor sum are what make the quantitative coupled result follow.

The overlapping-prefix calculation is not covered by the disjoint-letter run census or by the same-model terminal PGFs. checked_sources: Aguech–Abdelkader Theorem 4 and its future-height remark
value.rationale: The two heights interact through the same update symbols, so independent marginal laws and expected intensities are insufficient. The quantitative joint theorem shows that dependence does not persist in the critical window despite intersecting success predicates. It also gives control of counts, not just the maximum distribution, along with the correct discrete phase; this is a meaningful strengthening over terminal-altitude or one-coordinate analyses.
residual_risks: No claim for many coordinates, all thresholds, time-varying q, or continuous Gumbel convergence.
